Bathroom storage · Updated November 4, 2026

Good bathroom storage starts with a tape measure.

The most common storage mistake is a piece that does not fit: a cabinet that blocks the door, a tower too deep for the gap beside the vanity, an under-sink organizer that runs into the drain pipe. After fit come the material, since cheap MDF swells in a humid room, and the wall anchor that keeps a tall unit from tipping. We compare storage on those three points, using spec sheets, current Amazon prices and what verified owners report.

Our method

How we research

What we compare

  • Footprint: width, depth and height against the space you measured, including door swing and the toilet tank or drain pipe.
  • Material: powder-coated steel, solid wood and bamboo handle humidity better than laminated MDF, which swells once water gets in.
  • Stability: whether a tall cabinet or over-the-toilet rack ships with a wall anchor or anti-tip strap.
  • Price: Amazon's current price, checked every night.
  • What verified owners report after months of daily use.

What we don't do

We don't run a lab, and we don't claim to have installed or handled these products ourselves. Our picks come from published specifications, current Amazon prices and what verified owners report again and again.

Every Amazon link on this site is an affiliate link. It never decides the ranking.

Before you buy

Common questions

Over-the-toilet rack or floor cabinet: which is better?

It depends on what you can spare, wall or floor. An over-the-toilet unit adds shelves without using new floor space, but it is tall and top-heavy, so anchor it to the wall. A floor cabinet holds bulkier, heavier items and keeps them within reach. Our over-toilet vs floor storage comparison walks through the trade-offs.

What should I measure before buying bathroom storage?

The width of the wall or gap you want to fill, the ceiling height, the swing of every door nearby, and the toilet tank if the unit goes above it. For under-sink storage, measure the cabinet's inside width, depth and height, plus the position of the drain pipe, which is what keeps generic shelving from fitting. Our bathroom storage buying guide covers the rest.

Which materials hold up in a humid bathroom?

Powder-coated steel, solid wood, bamboo and solid plastic resist moisture well. Laminated MDF and particleboard cost less but can swell at the edges once water gets in, so keep them away from the shower and out from under a sink that might drip. Running the fan after a shower helps any material last longer.
